correctness.rationale: For every pair of distinct noncentral vertices u and v, the adjacent spokes cu and cv can only be distinguished by u or v, forcing all but at most one noncentral vertex into any local edge metric generator. The proposed size-rm-1 sets distinguish arbitrary adjacent edge pairs; the only case not handled by a selected noncommon endpoint is a spoke versus an internal edge whose other endpoint is the unique omission, and a selected vertex in a different blade gives edge distances 1 and 2. Thus the lower and upper bounds match and equality forces the stated complete basis family. The independent checker directly evaluates all adjacent edge pairs.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The present graph is obtained from a star on rm leaves by adding all clique edges within r disjoint groups of size m. That transformation creates many new adjacent-edge pairs, so the star result supplies only a suggestive lower-bound pattern, not an upper bound or optimizer classification. The new proof establishes that every one of those added constraints is still met by exactly the old minimum-set family.

value.rationale: Generalized windmills are a standard infinite clique-amalgamation family containing friendship graphs. The result gives the exact local edge metric dimension, classifies every basis, and counts all minima for all complete blade sizes. It identifies a genuine stability phenomenon under adding dense intra-blade edge sets to a star-like spoke system, a transformation for which local edge metric dimension has no monotonicity guarantee.
